The real efficiency improvements in a plant come at the other end. In a conventional steam power plant with, the entire generation chain is under vacuum. This is because basic physics - water boils and stays steam at lower temperatures under vacuum, so the lower your pressure, the longer your steam stays steam and the more work you can extract from it.

Colder temperatures mean colder cooling water, or in the case of an air cooled condenser, cooler air. This has the effect of ( with water seal vacuum pumps ) making the pumps run more efficiently, giving you a better seal and a better vacuum, for longer lasting steam. It also gives you colder cooling water for the condenser ( or colder cooling air ) which takes your remaining steam back to water more efficiently ( and hopefully with less binding in the condenser ) for feed back into the steam process.

All of this makes the system run at closer to peak performance and lessens the chance of a trip, or the pressure rising so high that the turbines can no longer operate because the steam isn't moving through the system.
